subject: Follow-up: EU residency + CMK options for FinServ use-case
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Anna Leclerc <anna.leclerc@finserv-eu.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: EU residency + CMK options for FinServ use-case

Hi Anna — thanks again for carving out 30 minutes today. Quick recap and next steps so we can align the security folks on the exact integration path for the POC: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary constraint: all inference inputs & logs for the regulated product must remain resident in the EU (no replication to non-EU regions).
- Encryption: in-transit TLS required (mutual TLS preferred at API edge), at-rest AES-256 required. Customer-managed keys (CMK) required for model input encryption for the sandbox and production flows.
- Logging: audit logs need to be retained for 7 years, with access controls and export to the customer SIEM.
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency target is 250ms for the interactive flow — want to validate once we pick the deployment footprint.

Open technical questions for you/security team (please confirm or correct):
1) Do you require HSM-backed KMS for CMKs during the POC or will a customer-managed cloud KMS (with BYOK import) suffice initially?
2) For the 7-year retention, do you expect Redwood to host that log store inside the same EU region or will you pull/replicate logs into an internal archive?
3) Any additional metadata that must be redacted from logs (e.g., full user identifiers vs. hashed IDs)?

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Camila will send a short CMK option playbook (HSM vs cloud KMS) and an implementation checklist. (Camila: can you attach the playbook + network diagram?)
- We’ll produce a scoped Demo Plan for an EU-only Dedicated deployment and include token-level cost estimate.
- Coordinate a 30–45 minute technical call between FinServ security and our infra engineer to lock down mTLS and KMS flow (suggest Tue/Thu next week).

Attachments: redwood-cmk-implementation-guide.pdf (high level), eu-network-patterns.png (sample VPC egress/ingress)

Thanks — Hannah

--

From: Anna Leclerc <anna.leclerc@finserv-eu.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:58:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: EU residency + CMK options for FinServ use-case

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our security team: 

1) HSM requirement: For production we do require HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 level 3 / eHSM equivalence). For the POC, we can accept a customer-managed cloud KMS instance as long as the key material is generated in our KMS and not exported. If you offer an import-only BYOK flow, that is okay for the early POC but we will still need to validate HSM path for the go-live.

2) Logs: Preferred pattern is that Redwood stores the immutable audit stream in the EU region and we subscribe via secure export to our SIEM (SFTP or secure push). For long-term cold storage we will pull daily archives into our internal vault. Please ensure logs can be labeled with environment and tenant id so we can filter.

3) PII redaction: We cannot have free-text user identifiers in log payloads. Hashed IDs with a keyed HMAC are acceptable, and we will provide the hashing spec in a follow-up.

Scheduling: Tue 13 Apr 09:30–10:00 CEST works for the security call. Please send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Anna

--
Anna Leclerc

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 12:20:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: EU residency + CMK options for FinServ use-case

Thanks Anna — noted. Brief tech notes and what we’ll surface in the technical call: 

- HSM path: Redwood Private supports HSM-backed key wrapping for CMKs via partner HSMs (we can demonstrate a representative KMS HSM flow — certificate attestation + remote signing APIs). For Dedicated we can offer a direct HSM connector in the customer VPC.
- BYOK/import: Supported for early POC workflows. We will document differences: key lifecycle, rotation windows, export policy (we prevent key export), and required IAM mappings.
- TLS: mTLS is supported at the API edge; we will provide the TLS cert exchange steps and our client cert rotation policy in the playbook.
- Logging & retention: Redwood can retain audit logs in the EU for the 7-year SLA; we support secure push to SFTP or push to customer SIEM over TLS. Logs can be emitted without free-text identifiers — we will implement an HMAC-based ID hash at ingestion if you provide the key.

I’m attaching the CMK playbook and a sample network diagram to this thread. Also raising one internal ask: Jordan — can you prepare a short note on token-cost impact for enabling per-request HMAC hashing (adds small compute + ingress parsing)?

Attachments: redwood-cmk-implementation-guide.pdf, eu-network-patterns.png, soc2-controls-extract.pdf

Cheers,
Camila

On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 12:20 PM CEST Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com> wrote:
> I’m attaching the CMK playbook and a sample network diagram to this thread. Also raising one internal ask: Jordan — can you prepare a short note on token-cost impact for enabling per-request HMAC hashing (adds small compute + ingress parsing)?

Quick cost note for the group: enabling per-request HMAC hashing on ingestion for PII redaction is lightweight — expect ~3–5% additional CPU on the inference frontends depending on batch sizes. For pricing, we’ll represent this either as a small usage uplift in the POC estimate or bundle it into a Dedicated instance CPU sizing. I’ll add a short table to the Demo Plan.

I’ll also create the calendar invite for Tue 13 Apr 09:30 CEST and include the call agenda (mTLS handshake flow, CMK import vs HSM path, log export pattern).

– Jordan
